Delivery Hero treats the pre-August 2021 Glovo Spain model as a probable risk and recognizes provisions for it, while the model in place since August 2021 is treated as only possible (not probable) and is disclosed as a contingency of € 440.0 to 770.0 million rather than provisioned.

- Provisions are recognized where a rider risk is more likely than not, which applies to the model operated by Glovo until August 2021 in Spain (and also Glovo Italy and Foodora France) [2].
- Where the risk is deemed possible but not probable, it is disclosed as a contingency — this applies to Glovo Spain after August 2021, Glovo Portugal, and PedidosYa in Argentina [2].
- For the post-August 2021 model, Spanish social security investigations led to a contingent liability of € 440 to 770 million disclosed in the notes, and no provision was recognized because reclassification by Spanish courts was assessed as not probable [1][6].
- Regarding the pre-August 2021 proceedings, during 2024 Glovo had to provide bank guarantees to Spanish courts to secure payment of the liabilities claimed by the authorities [3][4].
- Glovo decided in December 2024 to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain effective 2025, to avoid further legal uncertainties related to the model in place since August 2021 [3][5][7].

The commitment fell by 244.8m EUR (304.3m − 59.5m), from EUR 304.3m at the end of 2022 to 59.5m EUR at the end of 2024.
Approximately 850,000 riders worldwide delivered at least one order for Delivery Hero in 2024.

In 2024, Zalando evolved Zalando Plus from a paid membership to a free-to-join model with a points-based system rewarding purchases and engagement (e.g., newsletter subscriptions), with points unlocking four benefit levels; it was tested in Spain and expanded to France and Austria, with further rollout planned for 2025 (Group strategy, Key intangible resources, Foreword). At year-end, the report mentions increased accruals for the reimbursement of Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025, included in "others" within other current non-financial liabilities (Notes 9.-26., (24.)).

Vodafone Turkey - 2G licence extension: €120 million for a six-year extension until 30 April 2029 (excluding 18% VAT), paid in advance with a capital injection.
Turkcell - 2G licence extension: EUR 120 million (plus EUR 21.6 million of value-added taxes), paid in installments — an initial payment of EUR 81.6 million (down payment plus VAT) paid in TRY 1.7 billion during 2023, approximately half of the remaining installments amounting to EUR 31.1 million paid in April 2024 at TRY 1.1 billion, with the remaining amount to be paid within a year.

Both agreed to the same extension fee of €120 million (excluding VAT), but Vodafone Turkey paid it in advance via a capital injection, while Turkcell is paying it in installments in Turkish Lira.
